answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a copper as the anchor of the cost.
